must_fix.issue: Destination section hands every musician and sound question back with nothing on what a quote covers, deposits, or who is responsible for the music on the day (r2 lines 315-324). Accountability and money trust loss.
must_fix.fix: Add questions only, no answers or promises: for live musicians, ask what the quote includes (rehearsal, travel, set-up time, how long they play) and that it is confirmed in writing, plus the deposit and cancellation terms in writing; for sound, ask who supplies and operates the sound system at the ceremony, who on the venue side is responsible for the music on the day, and what happens if a musician, power or playback fails. No prices, fees, named musicians or who-to-ring claims.

must_fix.issue: First Concierge CTA sits mid-article straight after the modern list, before the destination evidence, and 'plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world' raises the commission question unanswered (r2 line 313); closing CTA offers 'the feeling you want' with nothing on how the fee works (r2 last line).
must_fix.fix: Remove the line-313 CTA or move it below the destination question list so the single primary CTA follows the evidence (per brief). Reword CTAs using brand-facts.md claims only: one Wedded Advisor as single point of contact; the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins; suppliers paid at standardised industry rates. Drop 'payments, anywhere in the world'. No fee amount, fee basis or commission figures. Keep UTMs.

should_fix.issue: Modern entries mostly end with a bare '*Suits:* the couple.' (r2 lines 255-279), so the scannable line stops helping readers choose, and the modern list feels generic.
should_fix.fix: Sharpen each modern 'Suits' line with setting, pace and live or recorded (for example acoustic guitar, string arrangement, beach or garden) using only what each entry and 03-source-pack.json already support. No lyrics, meaning claims or new songs.

consider.issue: Key takeaways name no songs; a searcher wants the answer in the first 100 words.
consider.fix: Add one takeaway naming three of the 40 by style, mirroring the bridal entrance FAQ: Bridal Chorus or Canon in D (traditional), Nuvole Bianche (gentle), A Thousand Years (modern). Strongly recommended for search intent.

consider.issue: Pace advice stops at one sentence; large wedding parties and long aisles get no timing help.
consider.fix: Add a short note for large guest lists and wedding parties: time the full walk at the rehearsal, let live musicians repeat a section, and ask the venue about amplification and ensemble size for a large ceremony space. No figures.

consider.issue: Church section is all Western hymns; nothing acknowledges families' own entrance customs.
consider.fix: One neutral line: if your families have their own cultural or faith customs for the entrance, talk to your celebrant and musicians early about how to include them. No named traditions, songs or sourcing claims.

consider.issue: No question on privacy around rehearsals and performers.
consider.fix: Optional venue question: can the ceremony space be closed to other guests while musicians rehearse and play? Question only.
